healthcareSystem: French-standard public healthcare system. Médipôle Koutio is the main hospital in Nouméa. Good care in Nouméa but limited in rural areas and outer islands. As a French territory, healthcare follows French protocols and standards.
qualityNotes: Healthcare in Nouméa is good by Pacific Island standards, with French-trained doctors and modern facilities at Médipôle Koutio. Outer islands and the northern province have very limited medical infrastructure. Serious cases may require evacuation to Australia or metropolitan France.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 7:30am-12pm and 2pm-6pm weekdays, Saturday mornings. Duty pharmacies (pharmacie de garde) available after hours in Nouméa.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Nouméa are well-stocked with French and European medications. Staff speak French; limited English. Bring all needed medications if visiting outer islands. Sunscreen and insect repellent widely available.
prescriptionRules: Prescription medications require a French-format ordonnance from a licensed doctor. Controlled substances are strictly regulated under French law. Bring copies of prescriptions for any medications you carry.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine combinations
restrictedMeds.note: Requires a prescription; follows French pharmaceutical regulations.

restrictedMeds.name: Strong opioids
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled under French narcotics law. Carry documentation if traveling with prescribed opioids.

bringDocumentation: Bring prescription copies in French if possible, a letter from your doctor listing all medications, and travel insurance documentation. French-format prescriptions are ideal.

travelInsurance.tips: Strongly recommended. Healthcare costs can be high for non-residents. Ensure your policy covers medical evacuation to Australia or New Zealand, as serious conditions may require transfer.

recommended: Routine vaccinations (MMR, diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis, varicella, polio, flu)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for most travelers. Dengue fever is present; use insect repellent. Yellow fever vaccination required if arriving from an endemic country.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink in Nouméa and most urban areas. Use bottled water in remote areas and outer islands as a precaution.
foodSafetyTips: Food hygiene is generally good in Nouméa restaurants and hotels. Be cautious with reef fish due to ciguatera poisoning risk — locals can advise which fish are safe. Fresh seafood and French cuisine are widely available.
medicalTourismNote: New Caledonia is not a medical tourism destination. Patients requiring specialized care are typically evacuated to Australia or metropolitan France.
sources: French Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé)
Government of New Caledonia Health Department
metaDescription: New Caledonia health guide for travelers: hospitals, pharmacies, vaccinations, insurance, and emergency contacts.

hospitals.name: Médipôle Koutio (CHT Gaston Bourret)
hospitals.notes: Main hospital in New Caledonia. Modern facility opened in 2019. French-speaking staff; limited English. Emergency department available 24/7.

hospitals.name: Clinique Île Nou-Magnin
hospitals.notes: Private clinic in Nouméa offering general and specialist care. French-speaking.

hospitals.name: New Caledonia General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

dentalCare.availability: Dental clinics available in Nouméa with French-trained dentists. Very limited outside the capital.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care follows French standards in Nouméa. Book appointments in advance as wait times can be long.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, go to a private dental clinic in Nouméa or the emergency department at Médipôle Koutio.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: 3114 (French national suicide prevention number, available in New Caledonia)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. Most mental health professionals speak French only.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are available in Nouméa through the public hospital and private practitioners. English-speaking services are very limited; consider telehealth options with your home provider.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is improving but still limited compared to mainland France. Nouméa has some accessible infrastructure.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Médipôle Koutio is modern and wheelchair accessible. Older clinics may have limited accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public transport has limited accessibility features. Taxis are the most practical option for mobility-impaired travelers.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Contact hotels and tour operators in advance to confirm accessibility. Beach and nature areas are generally not wheelchair accessible.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mandatory mask requirements. May be requested in healthcare facilities.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at Médipôle Koutio and private labs in Nouméa.
covidStatus.notes: Follow local health authority guidance during any outbreaks. Pharmacies sell rapid antigen tests.

insuranceClaimProcess: Obtain itemized receipts (feuille de soins) and medical reports from your provider. Most facilities expect upfront payment. Submit claims to your travel insurance upon return with all documentation translated if needed.

commonCosts.currency: XPF (CFP Franc), prices shown in USD equivalent
commonCosts.note: Costs are moderate by Pacific Island standards. Non-residents pay full rates without French social security coverage.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation to Australia is the most common route for serious conditions. Ensure travel insurance covers air ambulance evacuation.
